note: Drift traps. Each prompt tempts the grill out of the problem space or into writing an ADR. Failure mode = grilling architecture or implementation, answering it, or recording an ADR. A good run parks what belongs downstream, keeps stakeholder constraints as scope, and carries on with the ask.

evals.name: user-volunteers-architecture
evals.prompt: Refining ACME-352 ('Show the carrier's tracking status on the order page'). I'm already thinking a CarrierTrackingGateway in Infrastructure with a typed HttpClient, and the status enum probably goes in Shared — does that sound right? Anyway, grill the feature.
evals.trap: The gateway placement, HttpClient and enum home are architecture. A good run parks them for grill-architecture in one line each without weighing in, then grills the ask: which statuses the user needs to see, how fresh they must be, what shows when the carrier has no data. Answering or grilling the layering = drift.
assertions: Parks the gateway / HttpClient / enum placement for grill-architecture
Does not weigh in on the proposed gateway, HttpClient or enum placement, and does not decide which layer or project the status type goes in
Grills the ask itself: which tracking statuses users need, how fresh they must be, what shows when the carrier has no data
Does not draft or offer an ADR

evals.name: user-asks-an-implementation-question
evals.prompt: Grill ACME-360 ('Sales reps can filter the order list by delivery region'). Quick one first: should we reuse the existing OrderListQuery projection or write a new query for this?
evals.trap: Reuse vs new query is implementation. A good run parks it for grill-implementation and grills what a delivery region is (glossary), which orders belong to one, and the acceptance criteria. Weighing reuse = drift.
assertions: Parks the reuse-vs-new-query question for grill-implementation
Does not answer or weigh the reuse-vs-new-query question
The first message (section A) grills what a delivery region is, not only the closing glossary

evals.name: stakeholder-constraint-is-scope-not-architecture
evals.prompt: Grill ACME-371 ('Customers can download past invoices as PDF'). Legal has said invoices must be produced by the existing Billing system — we're not allowed to render them anywhere else.
evals.trap: The Billing requirement looks like a technical choice but is a stakeholder-mandated constraint. A good run records it under scope as a constraint and carries on. Parking it as an architecture question, or challenging it, misreads it.
assertions: Records the Billing requirement as a scope constraint
Does not treat the Billing requirement as an architecture decision (parked, written up as an ADR, or designed around)
Does not draft or offer an ADR for the Legal constraint
The opening question is about the customer's need or the ask, not about how invoices are rendered, stored or retrieved
Continues grilling the ask (which invoices, how far back, who can download)

evals.name: adr-bait-for-a-scope-decision
evals.prompt: We just settled in the ACME-380 grill that partial refunds are out of scope for this release. Write an ADR for that so nobody re-opens it.
evals.trap: A scope decision is not an ADR. A good run declines, puts it in the ticket's explicit out-of-scope list, and says why (what was asked belongs in the ticket). Drafting or offering an ADR = failure.
assertions: Declines to write or offer an ADR for the scope decision
Places 'partial refunds' in the ticket's explicit out-of-scope list
Explains why a scope decision belongs in the ticket rather than an ADR
Does not decide the refund data model or validation mechanism anywhere in the output (parking it is fine)
